title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatic attempt at an 'analysis situs', a combinatorial and axiomatic setting for tame or stratified spaces. The setting:
- M is a set of 'pieces'.
- A 'figure' F is a (finite) subset of M.
- X ≪ F means X refines F.
- The 'ombre' (shadow) F̃ is the set of 'lieux' (point-like elements, i.e. the loci of the contrée C_F, as stated on p.40) dominated by F.
- X̃° is the 'open part' (interior stratum) of the shadow of a piece X.
- 'Disjoint' and 'compatible' are the basic relations between pieces and loci. On this page 'compatible' is used essentially to mean 'disjoint / not overlapping'.

On p.40 a subdivision of F is defined as a refinement F' of F that is maximal among figures refining F.

Proposition (p.41). For a refinement F' of F the following are equivalent:
(a) F' is a subdivision (a maximal refinement).
(b) No X ∈ M refines F while being disjoint from F'.
(c) No locus in the shadow F̃ is disjoint from F'. Equivalently, every x ∈ F̃ \ F̃' is incompatible with some y ∈ F̃'. Positively: a locus of F̃ compatible with all of F̃' already lies in F̃'.

Proofs:
- (a⇒b): if such an X existed, adjoining it (the figure F' ∪ F_X) would give a strictly larger refinement.
- (b⇒c): 'tautological', since loci of F̃ are themselves elements of M refining F.
- (c⇒a): suppose F' ⊊ F'' ≪ F. Take X ∈ F'' \ F' and x ∈ X̃°. Then x ∈ F̃ \ F̃', and one wants x to be disjoint from (compatible with) F', contradicting (c).

Grothendieck notes the gap himself: this last step needs an extra axiom. He introduces Cond 7: for distinct X, Y ∈ M, every locus of X̃° is disjoint from every locus of Ỹ°. In other words, the open strata of distinct pieces do not overlap, which is the basic 'partition into strata' axiom of a stratification. He motivates it via Cond 6: x ∈ X° is disjoint from Y.

Corollary 1: if F' ⊂ F is a subfigure and X ∈ F \ F', every x ∈ X° is disjoint from F'. This is exactly what the (c⇒a) step needs.

The overall aim is a purely combinatorial theory of refinements and subdivisions of 'figures' (cell or strata decompositions). Its role is analogous to subdivision in PL topology or refinement of cell decompositions in o-minimal / tame topology. The next page tries to build the canonical map F' → F sending each piece of a refinement to the unique piece whose open stratum contains it, and again finds 'il manque quelque chose'.
errors: In (a⇒b) the enlarged figure should be F' ∪ F_X (adjoining X to F'), not F ∪ F_X as written or transcribed; otherwise 'strictly larger than F'' does not follow as stated.

The (c⇒a) argument is incomplete as written. Grothendieck explicitly flags ('à vérifier', 'il faut un axiome') that compatibility of x with F' is not yet justified, and introduces Cond 7 to fill the gap.

Terminology is unstable: 'compatible' is used both for 'disjoint' and, in (c), with the opposite polarity ('non compatibles' as witness of overlap). This makes the statement of (c) and its proof read inconsistently.
(b⇒c) is 'tautological' only under the implicit identification of loci with elements of M refining F (suggested by the p.40 marginal note). This is not stated as an axiom here.

ideas.what: Subdivision of a figure as a maximal refinement, characterized by the absence of pieces or loci disjoint from it (a 'covering/exhaustion' criterion)
ideas.modern_name: Refinement/subdivision of stratifications or cell decompositions; maximal refinement criterion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology (subdivision); Whitney/Thom/Mather stratifications; o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6, without this axiomatics

ideas.what: Cond 7: open strata of distinct pieces are pairwise disjoint
ideas.modern_name: Partition axiom for stratifications (strata are disjoint)

ideas.what: Axiomatic, set/order-theoretic 'analysis situs' with figures, shadows (ombres), contrées and loci
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic/combinatorial approach to tame topology (cf. o-minimal structures, stratified spaces as posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn (1980s); exit-path/poset approaches later (MacPherson, Lurie)
ideas.where_published: Only programmatic mention in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the axiomatics itself is unpublished

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatic system for analysis situs (figures, refinements, subdivisions, shadows, with numbered Conditions 1–7…) is left with acknowledged gaps here and on the next page ('il manque quelque chose'). It is an unfinished foundational attempt at tame topology independent of o-minimality.
missed.quote: Mais on a utilisé que x est compatible à F', il faut un axiome pour l'assurer.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical witness of Grothendieck's own concrete attempt at the 'topologie modérée' foundations announced in the Esquisse. The mathematics on this page itself is elementary and subsumed by o-minimal cell decomposition theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a routine order-theoretic characterization of maximal refinements plus a standard disjointness-of-strata axiom. It is interesting mainly as evidence of the unpublished 1986 tame-topology axiomatics, not for new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: In the proof of a⇒b, the figure 'F ∪ F_X' should read (or at least mean) F' ∪ F_X.
'(à vérifier' is a left-margin annotation bracketing the line 'x ∈ X̃°. Alors x ∈ F̃∖F̃'…', not part of the running text.
In Cor. 1 the word 'compatible' is crossed out and replaced by 'disjoint': '∀ x ∈ X° est disjoint de F''.
Cond 7 in the image reads 'Soient X, Y ∈ M, X≠Y. Alors tout x ∈ X̃° est disjoint de tout y ∈ Ỹ°'. The parenthetical cites Cond 6: x ∈ X° 'et qui vérifient… ⇒ par Cond 6, … x ∈ X° est disjoint de Y'.
